title: Lay out a biosafety cabinet's work surface for a cell-culture session
instruction: Set up the biosafety cabinet's work surface for a cell-culture session: the media bottle, the pipette tip box and the waste pan, laid out the way cabinet practice requires, then let go of everything.
context: Autonomous and robot-assisted laboratories are a route by which AI systems run biological experiments, and almost every cell-culture protocol starts by loading a Class II biosafety cabinet correctly: work well inside the front grille, keep the rear grille clear so air flow is not blocked, and put clean items on one side and waste on the other. Technicians (O*NET 19-4021, 29-2012) do this at the start of every session; a robot that cannot lay out the cabinet cannot run the protocol.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A biosafety-cabinet work zone fills x 0.25 to 0.55, y -0.30 to 0.30 on the table: a slotted front grille at x 0.25 to 0.35, a slotted rear grille at x 0.50 to 0.55, a back wall, and a glass sash raised to a 380 mm opening (loading position; drawn, no collider). Three items stand in a jumble on the front grille at x 0.29: a 250 mL media bottle (70 mm across, 140 mm tall with cap, 0.30 kg) at y 0.11, a pipette tip box (127 x 83 x 55 mm, 0.12 kg) at y 0.24 and a yellow waste pan (80 x 130 x 60 mm, 0.25 kg) at y -0.10.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand: (1) the media bottle stands upright with its whole footprint between x 0.35 and 0.50 (10 cm in from the front edge, rear grille clear) and at y > 0 (clean side); (2) the tip box, the same; (3) the waste pan, the same but at y < 0 (dirty side); (4) with 1-3, every two items at least 3 cm apart and no gripper pad within 3 cm of any item. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once every condition has held together for 1 s with every item within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when the second began; any lapse restarts it; step points stop at 0.8. 0 overall if an item tips over 45 degrees at any time or leaves the table.
reset_notes: Stand the three items on the front grille as in the setup, upright; cabinet fixed.
fidelity: Cabinet is a fixed mat, grille strips and back wall; the sash is drawn raised and has no collider (the robot's ready pose passes through it). Items are rigid, one box or cylinder collider each, sizes typical of lab consumables (not specific catalogue parts), friction 0.6/0.5. Air flow is not simulated: the grille rules are geometric. The 15 cm usable depth is the robot's reach, not a real cabinet's 50 cm.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (arms hovered, items never moved); demo: 1.0 (success at step 564, scripted demo on Isaac)
